source.title: Revisiting Self-Distillation
source.authors: M. Pham; Minsu Cho; Ameya Joshi; C. Hegde

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure content is flattened, so exact figure values are not recoverable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies self-distillation, test accuracy, and Hessian-based flatness, but does not test the listed memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or example-removal versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's self-distillation accuracy and flatness findings concern generalization, but it reports neither training error nor a train–test gap. Its Hessian measures are not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7. Cited prior-work results are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests self-distillation accuracy and Hessian-based flatness, which do not match V1–V8. In particular, Hessian trace and eigenvalues do not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, and the study does not compare generalization gaps or rank sharpness against norm- and margin-based measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' interpretation: self-distillation can improve strong teachers, repeated rounds need not improve students progressively, and flatter minima offer a possible explanation. Their universal first-round language exceeds Table 2's results, and their flatness explanation needs qualification because Table 3's first-round SVHN student improves accuracy while both Hessian measures increase.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains students with a self-distillation loss and reports test accuracy and Hessian flatness; it does not reproduce the interventions or measurements in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Data augmentation, architecture, distillation weight α, and distillation round are varied; reported student accuracy and flatness vary across these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 shows first-round accuracy increases in 11 of 12 configurations, with VGG16 without advanced augmentation at alpha 0.8 decreasing from 94.39% to 94.38%. Later rounds do not consistently improve accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-distillation often improves held-out accuracy, including for strong teachers, but improvements depend on configuration and need not accumulate across rounds.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6 reports lower first-round Hessian trace and largest eigenvalue on CIFAR configurations, followed by fluctuations. Table 3 instead shows SVHN accuracy rising from 95.23% to 95.94% while trace rises from 197.53 to 205.79 and largest eigenvalue from 9.24 to 11.200.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-distillation can improve accuracy alongside lower Hessian curvature, but improved accuracy does not consistently require lower Hessian curvature.

record.problems: The results concern self-distillation, not the claim's random-label memorization and generalization gap. Flatness is assessed with Hessian-based measures and does not establish a correlation with the training–test gap. Some results are available only in figures whose precise values are not recoverable from the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2's Round 2 and Round 3 values, SAM comparison values, and results in Tables 1 and 3 are not included. They concern subsequent self-distillation rounds, cited-work comparisons, or another dataset and do not report training error or the claimed train–test gap. Figure-only accuracy and flatness values were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance and dependence on tuning, weight decay, or switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that address them.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict applies to V1–V8. The absence of training-error measurements is specifically relevant to V7's gap comparison; it is not a general reason to exclude accuracy results from every version. The SVHN exception is already declared omitted under rows_left_out, so it does not require a missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out random-label accuracy.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No magnitude-aware weight perturbation measure or comparison of its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.

rows.subject: ResNet18 and VGG16
rows.operation_detail: Compared Hessian trace and largest eigenvalue between teacher and self-distilled students
rows.measure: Relative flatness by Hessian trace and largest eigenvalue
rows.value: The text states that a single round of self-distillation results in lower trace and largest eigenvalue than the teacher; later rounds fluctuate around the first-round student's values.
rows.note: The study reports flatness measures, not the magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or train–test gap specified by V7.
rows.check: Faithfully summarizes Section 6's stated CIFAR trend, but combines architectures, datasets, rounds, and two measures. Figures 4–5 cover both architectures on CIFAR-10; Figure 6 covers ResNet18 on CIFAR-100. This is not V7's measure and should not be generalized to SVHN, where first-round trace and largest eigenvalue increase.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
